Serko Raises Annual Revenue Guidance as Business Travel Stays Robust
By David Winning
SYDNEY--Travel-software provider Serko raised its forecast for annual revenue as business demand remains solid, overcoming headwinds that include the impact of the Middle East conflict.

Serko said it now expects total income of between 135 million New Zealand dollars (US$74.6 million) and NZ$141 million in the 12 months through March. That represents an upgrade on prior guidance for NZ$128 million-NZ$134 million.

"First-half momentum has carried into the second half, and Serko expects underlying growth to continue on a seasonally adjusted basis for the remainder of FY27," the New Zealand-based company said in a regulatory filing.
The outlook was provided alongside a net loss of NZ$870,000 for the six months through September, representing an improvement on the NZ$9.5 million loss achieved a year ago.
Serko reported free cash flow of NZ$8.9 million in its fiscal first half, but said it isn't likely to achieve as much in the six months through March.
"Second-half free cash flow is expected to reflect normal revenue seasonality and payment timing,  alongside planned investment in Serko.ai," the company said.
